the story (a message to a friend that ends in a crumpled note and a sad face) and its props (phone in hand, city, sun tower, satellite, tram, house, crumpled paper with heart, sad face) are the reference's subject and scenery; never copied. Setting and subjects come from the voice-over

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 (2 sheets, both viewed) and dense fps=8 sheets over the whole film (4 sheets, all viewed, because shots average about 1 s); scene detect gt(scene,0.3) found cuts or cut-like changes at 2.58, 3.63–3.88, 4.17, 7.29, 8.46–8.67 and 10.33–10.58 s; the other shot changes (0.5, 1.5, 5.3–5.4, 6.35, 9.85, 11.1 s) are carry-throughs, morphs or pixel dissolves placed from the dense sheets. Audio present but not analysed: whether cuts land on music beats is unverified

visual_language: Flat graphic-poster illustration in a strict three-colour palette (hot pink, near-black charcoal, bone cream) with fine film grain, soft radial gradients and glows, and almost no outlines except thin pink or cream accent lines. Most frames are flat, symmetric, centred posters with big negative space; three shots (r1-s2, r1-s9, r1-s10) switch to low-poly 3D with flat or soft gradient shading. Typography is almost absent: only a tiny chat bubble at the start and end; the story is told by images and one travelling object. Rhythm is very fast: 12 shots in 11.5 s (about 1 s each), never longer than 1.4 s; cuts, morphs, a circle match cut, a pixel dissolve and foreground wipes alternate, so the eye is always handed from one form to the next. Signature moments: the message leaving its screen and folding into a paper plane, the tower bursting into pink particles, the ring closing like an iris, the ribbon-to-triangle-to-road morph, the plane crumpling on impact, the glowing mark lifting off, the light cone that reveals a face, and the loop back to frame 0. Format is 9:16 and uses the full height (vertical pillars, towers, cones).
look: Mostly flat 2D vector poster (no perspective, solid fills, radial gradients, glow halos, film grain), with selected 2.5D and real low-poly 3D shots: a block-city fly-through in one-point perspective, a metallic device edge, a crumpled paper ball with soft gradient facets. Light is graphic, not physical: pink glows behind key objects, gradient rims on silhouettes, no cast shadows on flat frames. Materials: matte paper, matte vector fills, one brushed-metal edge. Depth comes from blurred foreground and background shapes (soft-focus spheres, foreground shards, speed streaks with motion blur). Backgrounds are flat colour fields, starfields or dark rooms, never photographic.
code_translation: Mostly code-native. Flat poster frames as SVG/canvas with radial gradients, a grain overlay and blur filters; particle bursts on canvas; shape morphs as SVG path interpolation; pixel dissolve as a mosaic (pixelate) filter for 2 frames; speed streaks as stretched blurred bars. Per D55 the 3D shots stay 3D: the corridor fly-through and the crumpled object are built in three.js with low-poly geometry, flat or soft-gradient shading, an emissive pink glow and depth of field as blur, never faked as flat shapes. Estimated buildable in code: about 85% (everything except the exact soft facet shading of r1-s10, which three.js approximates well).
continuity: One traveller carries the whole film: a small object leaves the first frame and passes through every shot, changing form at key beats (message → folded plane → crumpled ball → glowing mark).
The traveller changes form by refolding mid-flight or on impact, never by a cut.
Shape-to-shape match cut: push into a circle, cut on the brightest frame to a new shot built around another circle.
Shape morph bridge: one solid form flows into the next shot's layout (ribbon → zigzag → triangle → perspective road), with solid colour flips as the beat.
Exit-frame and enter-frame on the same direction: the traveller leaves one shot by an edge and enters the next from the matching side or through an opening.
Dark foreground wipe and pixel dissolve as the only non-object transitions.
The three colours swap roles between shots (pink sky / black ground, then black sky / pink road), which keeps one world while every frame looks new.
Bookend loop: the last frame repeats the first, so the film can loop seamlessly.
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy its story, its objects (phone, city, satellite, tram, house, crumpled note, sad face), its shot order one by one or its copy.
Shots average about 1 s with no text holds; Persian on-screen text needs its minimum hold time, so text shots must be longer than the reference rhythm; readability wins over pace.
The one-frame colour flash and 2-frame pixel dissolve are very fast; keep them short but check they do not read as render glitches, and avoid repeated full-frame flashes.
Reference colours map onto brand colour roles (pink = accent/primary role, charcoal = background role, cream = surface/ink role); never used as literal hex values.
The film is built for a silent-style loop; a voiceover film needs a logo outro, so the loop bookend becomes an echo of the opening before the outro, not a true loop.
Audio was not analysed; whether cuts sit on music beats is unverified.
